correctness.rationale: The assumptions and edge-label probability are explicitly fixed: p+q iid signed columns with uniform independent hashes into disjoint p- and q-row blocks. The signed-incidence graph proof gives full column rank if and only if each connected component is unicyclic with an inconsistent cycle parity, including parallel-edge cycles and attached trees; on success the normalized determinant magnitude is 2^(C-n/2). The exponential formula for vertex-labeled bipartite rooted trees has T_L=x exp(T_R), T_R=y exp(T_L), and the sign-weighted cycle-core series -u/4 log(1-T_LT_R). The exact logarithmic Jacobian 1-st under x=s exp(-t), y=t exp(-s) gives the displayed all-integer finite sum. The independent covariance determinant-moment identity verifies the normalization for every p,q. The standalone verifier exhaustively checks all hashes in 11 small block allocations, complete signed integer determinants in five allocations, and exact rational moment identities for one hundred allocations. Those finite checks supplement the all-size proof, not replace it.

value.rationale: Full-column-rank probability and the discrete nonzero Gram determinant distribution are natural, algorithmically diagnostic invariants for square coordinate-subspace sparse sketches. The all-size closed coefficient formula addresses the zero-oversampling reliability boundary and quantifies differences between block allocations, replacing an unquantified rank-risk phenomenon with exact small- and all-size benchmarks. This is not merely a known one-block collision substitution: two-block hashes require a signed unicyclic multigraph and its attached-tree enumeration. No generic singular-value or floating-point claim is made; those scope limits make the result a precise structural benchmark rather than unsupported practical accuracy advocacy.
